source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Select the boar from a litter born to the herd's best sow — the one that farrows the most piglets per litter with the heaviest piglets at weaning (5–8 weeks) — and always choose the fastest-growing male from that litter. Look for a long body from head to tail with well-rounded hams, evenly sized, well-formed testicles, and a sound gait (even toes, not walking on toes, correct leg angle). Castrating the strongest, healthiest male piglets from the best sows and selling them for meat instead of keeping them as future boars weakens the herd over time, as does breeding between male and female siblings.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
